description: EXAMPLE / PROPOSAL DATA. A worked serve-dispatch table assembled ONLY from measurements already published in the Gridbook repository, each row citing the document it was quoted from. It exists to make the ultraplan P5c constrained-Pareto path runnable and reviewable end to end; it is NOT a qualified serving model and no allocation shipped from it is release evidence. docs/lanes/nvfp4-cb/format-speed-policy.md §1: 'Per-layer or per-operator timing tables may generate candidate assignments. They are not final evidence.' Every number here is a single-box, mostly single-seed measurement on one GB10, transferred across models and shapes; the NATIVE-PARITY served protocol is the only thing that promotes an assignment. Replace this file with your own measured table before using the constraint axis for anything that ships.
notes: THE HEADLINE TRADE (gridbook docs/audits/ultraplan_perf_2026-08-01.md §6, P5c): at ~4.5 bpw, choosing FP8-CB over the native arm buys quality at a measured 1.44x dense-prefill cost. That is the 'prefill/dense_prefill_1400' arena below, and it is the trade the allocator is supposed to see rather than discover at the release gate.

NVFP4_CB HAS NO WHOLE-MODEL ROW, deliberately. No published measurement gives the default fp4-CB quality path (the BF16 bridge) a whole-artifact TTFT or decode number: audit §2(b) says every dense M > 8 and MoE T > 16 expands to BF16 and feeds an Ampere-schedule grouped GEMM, and the only published timings of that route are the per-expert grouped-GEMM microbenchmarks in the two 'moe_grouped_*' arenas. Those are metric=operator_ms and therefore never SLO-eligible. Consequence: an assignment containing NVFP4_CB CANNOT be certified against a prefill or decode SLO from this table, and the evaluator refuses instead of interpolating. That refusal is the honest state of the record, not a gap to paper over.

MoE expand is ~35% of MoE layer time at Laguna scale (gridbook docs/KERNELS.md, K1.1 discussion). That is a SHARE of layer time, not a ratio against a named reference route, so it is recorded here as a note and not as a row. A share cannot be divided by a denominator this table declares.

The 'dense_mid_m_*' and 'dense_large_m_1400_gemm' arenas have NO absolute reference (statistic=ratio_only_no_absolute): the published fused-vs-transient numbers are kernel ratios with no whole-model wall time behind them. They are kept because they are the only evidence for the fused mid-M lane's shape, and because they show its structural ceiling (0.22x at M~1400) in the same units as its wins. They can never satisfy an absolute SLO.

The native reference arm in the whole-model arenas is a MIXED NVFP4/FP8 compressed-tensors artifact, not pure NVFP4 (format-speed-policy.md §5: 'Published "native" reference artifacts are generally mixed NVFP4/FP8'). Both native families are therefore priced at the arena reference, and neither row is evidence that one of them alone would measure the same.

Statistics are declared per arena and are mostly 'single_seed_point_measurement'. Policy §3 requires streaming TTFT/ITL/TPS percentiles for release evidence. The evaluator stamps the mismatch when a p95 SLO is checked against a point measurement; it does not pretend the point measurement is a percentile.
